verdict.rationale: The core DBOS product is an open-source, Postgres-backed library with no separate orchestration server, so self-hosting is inherent — you just install the library and point it at your own Postgres instance (dbos-docs-2, dbos-docs-20, dbos-docs-35, dbos-gh-1). Docs also describe self-hosting the optional Conductor/DBOS Console on your own infrastructure via Docker Compose (dbos-docs-19, dbos-docs-34). Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation of self-hosted Conductor/observability working smoothly — community reports (dbos-comm-8, dbos-comm-11) note the web UI/observability layer historically wasn't open-source self-hostable, a caveat around the full platform even though the core library itself is trivially self-hostable.
